Web Design FAQs — What You Need to Know

  • Timelines depend on the type of site you’re building. Our Website in a Week experience delivers a polished Squarespace site in just one week, while fully custom websites typically take 5–7 weeks. We outline the full timeline upfront and guide you through each phase so the process feels clear and manageable from start to finish.

  • Squarespace is best suited for service-based businesses and content-driven brands that want a streamlined, easy-to-manage site with strong design flexibility. Shopify is built specifically for eCommerce and is ideal for product-based businesses that need inventory management, payments, shipping, and scalability baked in. We’ll help you choose the platform that best supports how you sell and grow.

  • ShowIt offers a high level of creative freedom and is best for brands that want a highly visual, editorial-style website. It does not have built-in eCommerce capabilities and uses WordPress on the backend for blogging, which makes it more advanced and flexible but also a bit more hands-on. Squarespace is more streamlined and all-in-one, with built-in eCommerce and an intuitive interface, making it a great choice for small businesses that want a beautiful site that’s easy to manage long-term.

  • Yes, and we want you to feel confident doing so! All of our websites are designed to be easy to manage, even if you’re not tech-savvy. You’ll receive instructional videos and two weeks of post-project support so you’re never left guessing once your site is live.

  • We provide copy guidance and strategic support, including website outlines, structure recommendations, and refinement of existing copy. Full copywriting is not included unless noted and can be added as an additional service with the help of one of our recommended copywriters. This approach ensures your messaging is clear, intentional, and aligned, without slowing down your timeline.

  • Yes! Every website includes foundational SEO setup, including page titles, meta descriptions, clean site structure, image resizing for performance, and keyword-informed alt descriptions to support search visibility. While this isn’t a full ongoing SEO strategy for web design for small businesses, it gives your site a strong, thoughtful foundation to be discovered and grow over time. If you’re curious about a more long-term and in-depth SEO strategy for your website, start the conversation here and we can build a plan that is catered to your more advanced goals.

  • Yes. All website projects require finalized logos, colors, and fonts before design begins. If branding isn’t complete yet, we recommend starting with a branding package first to ensure your website feels cohesive, intentional, and aligned from the start.

  • GREAT question, and one that’s important to clarify upfront, because these are the “fine print” items that can impact project scope, budget, and timeline. Depending on your needs, additional costs may apply for things like: font licensing and photography assets, professional copywriting, advanced SEO strategy, premium apps, website hosting and subscriptions, printing or production fees, and any revisions beyond the included rounds.

  • Start by reaching out through our inquiry form here and telling us a bit about your goals for web design and where you’re headed. We’ll take it from there, guiding you toward the right next step and making the process feel clear, supportive, and easy from day one.
